opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner-Society approached the High Court questioning the acquisition of subject land and sought consequential relief to declare the acquisition to have lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013.
The Writ Petition as well as the intra-court appeal, have been turned down primarily on the basis of the Constitution Bench decision of this Court in Indore Development Authority vs.
Manoharlal & Ors. Etc., 2020 (8) SCC 129.
In addition, the High Court has taken note of the fact that the land allegedly purchased by the petitioner-Society was never mutated in their favour.
In order to substantiate the claim, the petitioner-Society has now placed on record some documents along with photographs of the alleged houses constructed at the site after getting the site plan sanctioned from the competent authority.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Since no such material was placed before the High Court,
we are not inclined to entertain the same at this stage.
